objective: Gather directional signals on what shoppers in the Times Square area would pay for model kits and how often they would buy, to inform whether official-kit retail pricing could plausibly support high-rent operating costs.
targetSegment: Adults 18+ who visit or live/work near Times Square, Manhattan, and who have bought or seriously considered buying a plastic model kit (e.g., Gunpla, anime, sci-fi or vehicle kits) in the past 12 months, mixing tourists, casual buyers and regular hobbyists.

questions.text: Which best describes your relationship with plastic model kits?
options: I build kits regularly (several per year)
I build occasionally (one or two per year)
I have bought kits mainly as gifts or souvenirs
I have browsed kits but rarely buy them

questions.text: For a mid-sized model kit (roughly 1/144 to 1/100 scale), what price range would you typically expect to pay at a physical store in Times Square?
Compared with buying the same kit online, how much more, if anything, would you be willing to pay to buy it in person at a Times Square store?
options: Nothing more; I expect the same or lower price
I would not buy in a physical store

questions.text: How many model kits would you expect to buy from a Times Square model kit store in a typical year?
What factors, if any, would most influence how much you spend at a model kit store in this area?

neutralityNotes: Questions ask about price expectations, store premiums and purchase frequency without mentioning brands, authenticity or the decision-maker's preferred option, use balanced ranges including 'not sure' or zero choices, and results are AI-persona directional signals that cannot substitute for actual wholesale cost, rent and distributor data.
